analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Spyridakis is one of the best professors at Davis. I am a science major and took His111B for GEs, but loved the class so much I decided to finish the whole series. Grading is: 25% midterm, 25% term paper (around 8 pages long), 50% final. He gives study guides for the exams so they arent too hard. Go to class! His lectures are truly legendary.

If you didn't already have an interest in the ancient world, you can count on Professor Spyridakis to change that. Hands down my favorite prof. His lectures are amazing and the class itself isn't too difficult. There are assigned textbooks for the class (which can be helpful for the final paper) but if you go to class + take notes, you'll be fine!

Professor Spyridakis is an amazing lecturer. He is very passionate about what he is teaching and very funny. His class was an easy B! I wrote the research paper in one night. I did not sleep and turned it in thinking I was getting an F. I received an B-.  I got B's on both exams. I studied the night before for the exams.

Not the "easy" class it's purported to be.  At the very least, if you're looking for an easy A, you're taking the wrong class. Start the research paper early, as it's more work than it seems like and is graded by a TA/reader (who may or may not grade harshly).

UC Davis legend. Probably taught my dad. No visual aids; he just talks in his booming voice for an hour. Engaging, but the material can get old.  Needed to attend his class to succeed. Didn't need the books he "assigned." 1/3 MT, 1/3 Final, 1/3 Term paper. Put effort into studying the themes and your IDs. Pay your respects and take his class.

Best math professor I have had at UC Davis so far. Engaging class lectures, and always had a practice midterm or final prepared. Midterms and final had no surprises, very straightforward. My major has nothing to do with Biology therefore 95% of the topics in this class I have never heard of. With that said though all of them are very interesting to me. Literally no prior knowledge is needed. The readings can gets a bit tough not in terms of length but vocab. Overall, he's a really good professor, very understanding, would recommend.

Grade is based on attendance, participation, and a 5-10 page essay at the end of quarter. Weekly readings were interesting and he would go over them in class. The was the best professor I've ever had. She cares so much about her students; she was always making sure we were all caught up and offered extra help out of class. She does like leaving a lot of discussions/essays, but with her lectures it was all easy.

analysis.name: Michael Ziser
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 65 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ziser himself is actually a really good lecturer with a bright personality. But the reading load, plus the final along with the esoteric guidelines he has for assignments (eg; unclear when he wants you to be interpretive and creative, or analytical and professional), makes this a course you should only take if you have to as an English major.

Ziser is a mellow, easygoing guy, but he really knows his stuff. He does have a habit of being 5-10 minutes late to class and running over time by 5-10 minutes, but if everyone starts packing up he'll take a hint and wrap it up. The essays are straightforward but if you don't do the reading you'll bomb the final-- it's all IDing passages.

He was alright. He's not a 'bad' professor. The other reviews are just correct that the workload is heavy. When he says you'll be spending 20 hours reading outside of class...guys, he's not kidding. Overall, enjoyable class and professor. But by the end, you have bad reading fatigue. Keep that in mind when taking one of his class. Good, but heavy.

Look, the professor is a nice guy. I don't have any problems with him or his TAs. But the final was unreasonable. To be expected to not only remember over 50 readings but to also remember their exact context, is impossible. The final is basically just luck—if you get lucky and get readings you remembered the best. Start memorizing them immediately.

Ziser's a good guy who's very passionate about the material. But there's A LOT of reading at a fast pace; you'll be reading entire novels in a couple of days. The final is cumulative and based on memorization; even though you're allowed a cheat sheet, a lot of people from my class still struggled. I'd only recommend if you're an English major.

analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Quite honestly one of the chillest grad student teachers there is.  Usually they are the hardest professors, but Zoller is very nice and helpful if you ask him questions.  Class it geared around creative expression which is nice considering its a research-paper course.  Final paper is graded very harshly compared to the other assignments.

Took him for AMS 130. One of the best grad student professor's! He was super relaxed and a really easy going guy. Explains exactly what his expectations are and will answer any questions you have! Expect about 6 short essays, zero tests, and lots of reading.  No midtern and the final is an essay. Would definitely take him again!

Took the class for a fun GE in the summer, and it was great. Karl was suuuuuper laid back, very easy going. He was clear about what he wanted out of us and what was going to be on the tests. Pretty straightforward class, would definitely take something taught by him again. Can't recommend him enough.

review_highlights.comment: Michele is one of the nicest teachers I have had at Davis. She cares about her students, and as long as you do all the assignments you'll get an A. She gives extra credit, and is extremely reasonable if you cannot turn in an assignment on time. Sweet lady, take her you will love it I promise you.

Best professor I've had thus far!Professor Zugnoni gives informative lectures and clear grading rubrics. There are weekly writing prompts that were short and relevant to the material. For each project we would peer review another classmate prior to turning it in. The class has a variety of assignments so you can excel in different areas. Pick her!
great one of the best ive ever hard at davis. Usually gives clear instructions and gives starightforward infromation

analysis.name: MacIej Zwieniecki
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Z's lecture style is informal and generally unorganized. He prepares images beforehand but goes in an unpredictable order, explanations are often unclear, and few words on slides make it hard to review content. He does do demonstrations with plants, gets the class laughing, and has a low workload, but nobody knows what's going on half the time.

This class was graded on a midterm and a final, lab/discussion participation, and a lab test. I honestly did not get anything out of this class because it was all just memorizing for tests. Prof. Z's test was extremely easy though if you memorize the definitions for the multiple choice test.

Professor Z is an eccentric and funny lecturer. Although he's not the most organized lecturer, I learned a lot from him. He's very passionate and knowledgeable about the material and is always willing to clarify. His exam for the first half of the class was glossary-based. He's a very kind grader.
Funny guy. The midterm is one question, not difficult. His lectures are WAYYY more detailed than they needed to be. When taking notes, just pay attention to the plant adaptations.
He is a very funny guy and makes class enjoyable. His test consists on designing a tree which is not too difficult. He goes over way more material than what you need to know for the midterm.

analysis.name: Zubair Shafiq
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took the virtual version of 32A. I didn't always attend his Zoom lectures because the Zybooks readings would cover the same thing and it felt redundant. He gives lots of HW, be sure to start in advance! Quizzes were fine. The AI projects at the end were annoying bc of unclear grading criteria but they fixed that and gave points back.

Professor Zubair is one of the best lecturers at Davis, if not the best. Go to his lectures, pay close attention and ask questions when you don't understand and he will answer. Weekly quizzes, piece of cake if you put a bit of studying. Final was difficult. HW assignments are very difficult, but extremely leniently graded. 10000000% recommend

Homework assignments take an ungodly amount of time. Quizzes every week. He's extremely unsympathetic and condescending. If you absolutely need to take the class with him (which was the case for me) it isn't impossible but if you have a choice I would avoid him.

The professor is really invested in the topic and has amazing lectures. You surely be able to benefit out of his teaching style during your career. The only problem I could see was the TA's were AI experts, and programmed all the projects using CHATGPT. The quizzes were easy, the final was tough(but curved), the projects and TA's were just terrible

Maybe it's my emotions speaking, but I have an 89.97%, with an unfair grading on my final project. I messaged both the professor and TA, asking for a question regarding the project, and was ghosted on both fronts. 
Great professor, amazing class, but lack of communication in the end was annoying. 
Overall, would take and recommend.

analysis.name: Nicolas Zwyns
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zwyns is an amazing professor. He's funny, he really knows his stuff, he does his best to make class interesting with his cheesy jokes. I loved his TAs as well. This class was tough and a lot of work but not too overwhelming or difficult. Lab was mandatory but easy and again, loved my TA. I definitely recommend this class and this professor.

Very interested in anthro (esp. stone tools), but expects you to learn lots of unnecessary info (locations/discoverers of each species, etc) so be prepared to study. He has a strong Belgian accent too, so beware if you'll have a hard time understanding. Term paper wasn't too bad. Lab is mandatory, lecture isn't, and he doesn't post study guides.

Professor Zywns is a really nice guy. Hes a pretty funny lecturer and a very fair grader and test giver. Hes pretty disorganized though, but you can tell he cares. The labs were easy but the practical was a bit tricky. I didnt take any notes in class and Im getting an A. Pretty easy if you put in a minimal amount of effort.

I have taken 2 classes with Zwyns. Goodness, the amount of headaches I had bc of his organization in lectures & on canvas is actually hilarious. He gave a French analogy of a topic I did not understand... why would I understand it in French if I dont understand it in English? He is super passionate on the topic(s), but its rough with him as a prof

This class is 5 units so expect to work for that extra unit. The tests are tough but the reading is not mandatory so it gives you more time to study the lecture pdfs that he puts online. Lab is chill. Had to study A LOT but I also learned a lot. Dr. Zwyns is a good guy who wants you to do well. Lectures are interesting and his accent isn't bad.
